annotations.text:
Nesting is the whole idea.
Indented steps happen DURING
the step above them.

One parentStepId reads three ways:
a bracket here, a drag handle in the
editor, a "meanwhile" list while cooking.

Two kinds of note, never merged.

The author's tip lives on the step.
Yours pile up with dates.

They meet on the cooking screen --
that pairing is why they are two
columns and not one.

Going without an ingredient hides
any step that used only that.

The estimate moves only when a MAIN
step drops -- a nested one happens
inside another step's time.

Cooking then carries a "without
carrots" marker, because the skipped
steps vanish silently.

The app never opens the link.
The user's own AI watches the video.

The prompt is the hard part: it has to
teach a stranger's model what nesting
is, or imports come back flat.

Cooking progress is stored on the
phone, so kitchen wifi dropping
cannot interrupt a cook.

Several recipes can be part-way
through at once.

Provider buttons are drawn plain here.
Real ones must follow Google's and
Apple's branding rules -- the one
place the design system does not win.
